evals.prompt: Context is getting full; prepare for /clear. All my subagents have returned.
evals.expected_output: Checks itself, without asking, that no agent or background task is running (ListAgents, a process scan, background Bash and Monitor tasks), runs `python3 -I dev/handoff.py write --agents-done` (dry-run first when the template changed), then `check --agents-done --json`, reports go/no-go with the finding list and prints the plain `dev/handoff.py start-command` output (a fresh `claude -n <name> --session-id <uuid> "..."` command); never edits task_plan.md by hand.
expectations: Verifies with ListAgents and a process scan that no agent is running and never asks the user whether agents are running
Runs dev/handoff.py write before check and reports both exit codes
Reports go only when check exits 0 and lists every P1/P2 finding otherwise
Prints the start command from dev/handoff.py start-command, run without --name
Tells the user to type /session-resume <name> only on the /clear and by-hand paths, never after the whole start command
Does not hand-edit task_plan.md, progress.md or the HANDOFF file

evals.prompt: Checkpoint the session: a merge is still in progress and I have one implementer still running.
evals.expected_output: Stops at step 1 with a no-go: ListAgents shows the running implementer, so it reports that agent and the in-progress merge as what must finish, does not pass --agents-done, does not run write, and does not tell the user to /clear or /quit.
expectations: Does not pass --agents-done while an agent is running
Does not run write and stops at step 1 with the running implementer named
Names the in-progress merge as unfinished work (H.git-op-in-progress once check runs)
Returns no-go and does not tell the user to /clear or /quit

evals.prompt: handoff: put the R-176 release intake first in the next session's action, and the user still owes R-173 and R-056.
evals.expected_output: Edits references/handoff-template.md (the action section leads with the R-176 intake, the owner section holds no session name), copies it to the .agents mirror, confirms R-173 and R-056 are `owner user` lines of `## Open requests` (the generated Pending user line carries them), runs write --dry-run to show the diff, then write and check, and prints the plain start command with its generated name.
expectations: Changes the template rather than the generated block
Puts the user-owed items in `## Open requests` as `owner user` R-n lines (R-173, R-056), never in the template
Leads the action section with the R-176 release intake
Syncs the .agents/skills/session-handoff mirror after the template edit
Shows the write --dry-run diff before writing
The start command comes from dev/handoff.py start-command and its name is not the current owner's

evals.prompt: I'm upgrading Claude Code to the new version, so I'll /quit and start again. Prepare the handoff; one of my Monitor tasks is still watching a build.
evals.expected_output: Treats the Monitor task as running work (exit force-kills background commands 1.5 s after it stops): reports no-go until the task finishes or is stopped on purpose, then runs write and check, sets the CLI row from `claude --version`, puts the release intake first in the action, prints the plain start command and offers the /quit path (ignore the printed resume line, paste the start command, type nothing else) and the by-hand path (paste without the prompt, then /reload-skills, /reload-plugins without --force, /session-resume <name>), telling the user to use one.
expectations: Counts the Monitor task as running work and does not go until it has finished or been stopped
Sets the state-rows CLI row from claude --version and leads the action with the pending release intake
Prints dev/handoff.py start-command without --name
Offers /quit then paste the start command, and says to ignore the claude --resume line /quit prints
Offers the by-hand path /reload-skills, /reload-plugins (never --force), /session-resume <name>, and says to use one path, never two
